results.query: What are the hard hat requirements and PPE rules for workers in Zone Alpha?
results.answer:
According to standard plant safety protocols (OSHA 1926.100(a)):

• [SOP-PPE-001 — Industrial Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Compliance Standard]: All personnel, contractors, and visitors entering active industrial fabrication zones or heavy construction areas must wear Type I or Type II hard hats conforming to ANSI/ISEA Z89.1-2014. Hard hats must be inspected daily for cracks, dents, and suspension strap degradation. In designated Zone Alpha and overhead crane operating envelopes, Class E (electrical rated up to 20,000V) or Class G (rated up to 2,200V) hard hats are mandatory. Personnel detected without safety helmets in restricted zones must be immediately alerted, and work must halt until compliance is restored.

• [SOP-ZONE-002 — Restricted Zone Entry and Dwell Time Protocols]: Restricted hazardous zones are demarcated by physical barriers or calibrated virtual bounding polygons. Unauthorized pedestrian entry into high-risk machinery zones triggers an instantaneous Level-1 ZONE_ENTRY security alert. If a worker remains stationary or idle within a restricted boundary for greater than 5.0 consecutive seconds (displacement < 20 pixels), an IDLE_ALERT event is dispatched to control room dispatchers. Prolonged idle dwell indicates potential worker incapacitation, entrapment, heat exhaustion, or unauthorized lingering near high-voltage busbars.

• [SOP-VOLT-004 — High Voltage Safety Clearances and Flash Boundary Standards]: Electrical distribution transformers (such as EQ-TX-8804 operating at 11kV/433V) and MV switchgear panels (EQ-SWG-3310 operating at 17.5kV) possess a Minimum Approach Distance (MAD) of 3.0 meters for uninsulated personnel. Arc flash protective boundaries extend 1.5 meters from exposed energized terminals. Arc-rated face shields (minimum 12 cal/cm² rating) and voltage-rated rubber insulating gloves with leather protectors (Class 2, rated up to 17,000V AC) are required for testing or voltage verification.

Applicable Enforcement Zones: zone_alpha_danger, crane_envelope, fabrication_bay.

results.query: What is the proper Lockout Tagout (LOTO) procedure before servicing an induction motor or pump?
results.answer:
According to standard plant safety protocols (OSHA 1910.147):

• [SOP-LOTO-003 — Hazardous Energy Control: Lock-Out / Tag-Out (LOTO) Procedures]: Before conducting maintenance, servicing, or inspection on rotating machinery (such as induction motors EQ-MOT-7041 or centrifugal slurry pumps EQ-PMP-2093), workers must enforce zero-energy state isolation under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147. All circuit breakers must be switched to OFF, physically locked with designated safety padlocks, and tagged with the technician's identification and timestamp. Residual electrical charge in drive capacitors (such as 480V Yaskawa GA-700 drives) must be discharged and verified with a calibrated multimeter before physical touch.

Applicable Enforcement Zones: motor_control_center, pump_house, substation.
